ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZi6ddg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDJqNI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 65, "title": "Add optional MSX2 MSX-MUSIC with clocked YM2413 audio and independent firmware mapping", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `c54482e0153ad15db8e79888c81258515e085169`, `Hardware::output` has no MSX-MUSIC ports and the audio path mixes only PSG/SCC. Software cannot use YM2413 music or discover independently installed FM firmware. This is a complete hardware omission affecting FM-capable software; no commercial-title failure was observed.

## Expected outcome

Provide one explicitly optional **internal-style MSX-MUSIC profile for MSX2**: clocked YM2413 synthesis, write-only ports 7Ch/7Dh, and separately supplied 16 KiB firmware in expanded slot **3-1**, addresses 4000h–7FFFh. Keep the game cartridge in slot 1, disk interface in slot 2, sub-ROM in 3-0 and mapped RAM in 3-3.

Include nine melodic channels, fifteen preset instruments plus the programmable instrument, and six-melody/five-percussion rhythm operation. Mix FM into the existing native/Wasm/browser audio stream. This optional device does not change the machine generation.

## Context

Relevant paths are `crates/msx-core/src/{lib,psg,firmware}.rs`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, browser firmware/import/audio code, existing audio and Philips integration tests, and distribution/provenance tooling.

The [MSX-MUSIC hardware chapter](https://map.grauw.nl/resources/datapack/Vol2-3.1MSX-MUSICHardware.pdf) distinguishes internal ports from FM-PAC memory registers and enable controls. It documents software identification and minimum write spacing. [Pinned openMSX MSXMusic.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/MSXMusic.cc) corroborates separate firmware mapping, reset and timed I/O. Slot 3-1 is this repository's selected placement, not a claim to reproduce an entire historical machine.

[YM2413 manufacturer-derived documentation](https://d4.princess.ne.jp/msx/datas/OPLL/YM2413AP.html), [physical-chip experiments](https://www.smspower.org/Development/YM2413ReverseEngineeringNotes2018-05-13), and [emu2413 at a1d5120](https://github.com/digital-sound-antiques/emu2413/blob/a1d5120903b75f93d3eb7690e34a29c0b4add903/emu2413.c) provide synthesis references. The transcription mixes documentation with analysis; experiments and upstream models retain discrepancies. Exact analog output and undocumented write-edge behavior remain uncertain.

Saved cassette validation reports 261 Rust and 174 browser passes; inspected CI metadata marks native/browser checks successful. These existing results contain no FM coverage. Tests were not rerun during planning. PR #64 records source self-review but retains pending PR-review wording.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add the complete selected YM2413 synthesis profile in portable Rust: 3.579545 MHz clock, clock/72 internal output cadence, channel pitch/volume/key/sustain controls, two-operator modulation and envelopes, programmable/preset instruments, feedback, waveform selection, key scaling, AM/vibrato, and all five percussion voices with noise. Document approximations and register alias/reserved/test behavior supported by inspected evidence. A generic oscillator or nonzero-audio stub is insufficient.
- [ ] Route 7Ch address and 7Dh data writes using existing low-byte port decoding; normal reads retain unconnected FFh behavior. Installed internal-style I/O and synthesis remain active when its ROM slot is hidden. Preserve ordered writes and phase across instruction/frame boundaries; document instruction-level timing. Exercise valid streams respecting at least 12 chip clocks after address writes and 84 after data writes. Document a deterministic policy for faster writes without claiming unspecified silicon behavior is established or adding automatic CPU waits without evidence.
- [ ] Add transactional core/Wasm/browser installation and removal using an explicitly selected 16 KiB internal-profile firmware image. Map its exact bytes read-only only in slot 3-1/page 1; do not inject production identification strings or implement host-side FM-BIOS shortcuts. Installation/removal restarts selected firmware while retaining cartridge/SRAM, installed disk interface and disk changes, cassette, and system firmware selection. Reset retains installation and clears chip state. Existing firmware/cartridge transitions retain installation. On MSX1, retain the image inactive with no FM decoding/output; returning to MSX2 resets/reactivates it. Explicit removal disables the device. Preserve existing model-transition behavior for other media.
- [ ] Cover absent/present hardware, slot boundaries, FFFFh secondary-slot precedence, ROM protection, reset, hidden-ROM sound continuity, repeated data writes, channel independence, custom-instrument updates, preset selection, envelope/key transitions and rhythm switching. Check exact clock/sample counts and equivalent PCM for differently partitioned elapsed cycles, including long runs.
- [ ] Use independently specified expectations: custom-sine pitch from clock/F-number/block arithmetic, volume/envelope bounds, channel/rhythm distinctions, and short deterministic PCM/reference traces with recorded provenance and justified numerical tolerances. Derive expectations independently of production routines; nonzero/finite samples alone do not establish synthesis correctness. Show representative new assertions fail against the missing baseline path.
- [ ] Supply original redistributable Z80 diagnostics and an explicitly identified diagnostic firmware fixture. Execute slot discovery, reads/calls through the installed fixture and normal OUT instructions; assert exact RAM/video results and FM output. Test simultaneous cartridge or SCC-I, Philips disk transfers, PSG and FM. No genuine FM BIOS, commercial ROM, human gameplay or physical hardware is a merge prerequisite; authored fixtures do not establish vendor FM-BIOS compatibility.
- [ ] Preserve the existing 44.1 kHz audio ABI, sample counts and disabled-device PSG/SCC output. Verify bounded finite combined output, continuous phase while registers are hidden or browser playback is muted, pause, reset and removal. Add compiled-Wasm/browser checks at `/` and `/msx-rust/` for real file import, CPU execution and scheduled PCM, audio controls, malformed/allocation failures, canceled/stale imports and privacy. Reuse existing SRAM/export safeguards and allocation-failure methodology.
- [ ] Keep the core dependency-free and browser-independent. Independently implement from behavioral references or audit any compatible licensed adaptation, retaining required notices and provenance. Update relevant compatibility/profile documentation, firmware notices and distribution inventory. Preserve bundled firmware ownership, local-file privacy and existing disk/SRAM persistence behavior. MSX1 FM expansion, FM-PAC banking/SRAM, MSX-AUDIO, full VRAM/CPU timing work and BASIC language additions remain subsequent scope.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, using README setup where needed. Record failures, fixes and unperformed optional checks accurately. Complete source-Issue/full-diff PR review and resolve blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Compare additional register traces with a pinned reference implementation or physical YM2413. Exercise already lawfully available internal FM firmware and FM-capable software, recording exact inputs and observed results. These checks were not performed during planning and are not required for merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
